name: Strike Lab: Solo Combo Training Arena
request: Create a small, playable Strike Lab fighting-game training arena for one player on desktop and touch. Include a humanoid training dummy, a three-hit light-attack combo with visible windup, contact and recovery animations, synchronized hit sound effects, a visible accepted-hit counter and dummy health. The server must validate attack timing and range. Each accepted strike damages and counts once at contact; swinging out of range, holding the button or spamming during recovery must not create extra hits. Show distinct hit and miss feedback. After defeat, reset the dummy and let the player practice again; provide a clear reset control and an uncluttered arena. Search Marketplace first for complete reusable combat/training components, compatible dummy rigs, existing animations and sound rather than rebuilding everything. Inspect compatibility, behavior and included media, preserve useful working pieces and author only missing integration. Source missing audio from Marketplace and verify actual playing animations and audible sounds. Record an importer capability gap honestly rather than treating it as a bad asset. Choose reasonable styling and damage values yourself. No PvP, matchmaking, saving, monetization or large world. Success needs native evidence for the full combo, exact counting, misses, recovery spam, defeat/reset and desktop/touch controls. A damage script with a static dummy does not meet the animation requirement.

assetNeeds.role: Discover a complete reusable fighting or training component before deciding which combat behavior, dummy behavior, animation playback, media, and interfaces must be authored.
assetNeeds.constraints: Must fit a solo dummy-training loop and remain inside the supplied namespace. Inspect all scripts, remotes, dependencies, humanoid assumptions, combo timing, hit validation, included animations, included sounds, and unrelated PvP or monetization behavior. Preserve only audited useful features; unsupported serialization or importer behavior is a capability gap. No numeric require IDs or arbitrary HTTP code.

Humanoid dummy health and reset behavior

Inspect scripts, joints, ownership assumptions, collision, animator setup, animation references, reset behavior, and external dependencies. Remove no unrelated place content.

intent.interaction: The player approaches and attacks it; accepted contacts damage and animate it once, misses leave it unchanged, defeat briefly disables it, and reset returns it to its station.

assetNeeds.constraints: Must contain inspectable animation assets or preserved animation references compatible with the selected player rig and Marketplace permissions. Import/preservation failure is blocking and must be reported; do not substitute static poses or tweens.

intent.experienceRole: Makes the three-hit light combo readable as a fighting-game action rather than a static damage script and provides timing evidence for authoritative contact windows.

intent.experienceRole: Confirms the exact accepted contact moment and helps the player understand successful spacing and timing independently of the HUD.

assetNeeds.constraints: Must have retained provenance, load successfully, play through a supported audio instance, and pass native listening verification. Keep it concise, non-musical, and compatible in loudness with the light impact. No procedural, generated, placeholder, or invented-ID fallback.

spec.assetStrategy:
Begin with the optional complete combat/training Model because it may already contain compatible combo state, server validation, dummy behavior, animation markers, sounds, input, or HUD interfaces. Inspect its full hierarchy and sources before deciding that those systems are missing; do not strip embedded behavior merely to satisfy a static importer. Independently inspect a compatible humanoid dummy candidate so rig, joints, Animator, collisions, reset assumptions, and animation compatibility are known before integration.

The requested animated loop and audio are mandatory. Since standalone Animation retrieval is unsupported by this adapter, search required Models containing the three player attack animations and dummy reaction/defeat animations. Verify their references, permissions, target rig, markers or contact timing, and actual native playback. If the importer cannot preserve those assets or their necessary hierarchy, report the precise capability gap and block completion rather than substituting static damage, tweens, or invented animation IDs.

Audit retained complete components for captured impact sounds first, then fulfill any missing sound obligations through the separate light-impact and third-hit Audio searches. Every retained or separately sourced sound must keep provenance and pass load, playback, synchronization, and listening checks. Generated, built-in, procedural, placeholder, and silent fallbacks are prohibited.

Only after inspection should exact integration scripts and shared interfaces be assigned. Preserve useful verified component behavior and media, remove or disable only audited out-of-scope features such as PvP or monetization within the supplied namespace, and author the minimum missing server validation, state replication, controls, HUD, lifecycle cleanup, and feedback glue. Optional complete-system or dummy acquisition may use the bounded fallback policy only after documented unsuccessful discovery and inspection; required animation-bearing Models and Audio remain blockers if acquisition or verification fails.
spec.title: Strike Lab: Solo Combo Training Arena
spec.summary:
Create a compact, single-player fighting-game practice lab centered on one server-authoritative humanoid dummy. From a safe spawn, the player immediately sees a raised octagonal training mat, the dummy at the far target mark, a concise HUD showing dummy health and accepted hits, and clearly labeled Attack and Reset controls. The short approach lane teaches spacing: attack near the dummy to land strikes, or attack from outside range to observe distinct miss feedback. Desktop uses a primary attack binding and reset key/button; touch uses large, separated on-screen Attack and Reset buttons.

The core action is a three-step light combo. Each step visibly moves through windup, contact, and recovery. A request starts an attack only when the server-authoritative sequence permits it; contact is evaluated once at a server-controlled contact time. A valid in-range contact deals damage, increments the accepted-hit counter exactly once, plays synchronized impact audio, flashes hit feedback, and causes a visible dummy reaction. An out-of-range contact produces miss feedback without damage or count changes. Holding Attack does not auto-repeat, and new requests during recovery are rejected without producing additional contacts. Reasonable defaults are 100 dummy health, combo damage of 10/12/18, a short continuation window, and a slightly stronger third-hit presentation; exact timing may be adapted to verified Marketplace animation markers while preserving clear phases and server validation.

Dummy defeat produces a brief defeated state, then automatically restores the dummy so practice can continue. The accepted-hit counter remains useful across automatic dummy restorations, while the explicit Reset control immediately restores health, clears transient combat state, and returns the accepted-hit count to zero. Character respawn also clears stale attack state and safely rebinds controls and HUD state. No PvP, matchmaking, persistence, monetization, progression system, or large explorable world is included.

Marketplace discovery and inspection precede implementation decisions. Complete combat/training systems are evaluated before replacement code, followed by compatible humanoid rigs, animation-bearing models, and audio. Useful audited behavior, rigs, animation markers, and media are preserved. Script ownership and exact glue paths remain discovery-dependent until imported hierarchies, source code, dependencies, rig compatibility, and media provenance are inspected. Standalone animation retrieval is unsupported by the current adapter, so required animation discovery targets Models containing compatible animation assets; inability to preserve or import those animations is reported as a blocking capability gap, not treated as asset failure or permission to substitute static/procedural motion.
spec.visualDirection:
Use a clean near-future sports-science lab rather than a featureless floor. The playable area is a compact rectangular room approximately 46 by 34 studs with a safe collidable spawn pad, a short illuminated approach lane, and a central octagonal training mat. Low boundary rails and wall panels communicate the arena limits without obstructing the camera. The dummy station sits on a contrasting target ring about 12 studs from spawn, keeping traversal under a few seconds. A reset console or clearly marked reset zone sits off the mat edge so it is visible but does not compete with the attack target.

Favor simple beveled silhouettes, dark charcoal flooring, pale structural panels, and restrained cyan lighting. Use warm orange only for attacks and accepted-hit feedback, red for low health/defeat, and cool gray or blue for misses and neutral state. The humanoid dummy should be readable against the backdrop, with a strong torso/head silhouette and a grounded target marker. Lighting should keep both player and dummy poses legible without excessive bloom, fog, clutter, or animated decoration.

Attack presentation must communicate gameplay timing. Windup shows an anticipatory pose and restrained attack cue; contact aligns the striking pose, server result, impact sound, brief dummy flinch, and compact hit flash; recovery visibly returns the character toward guard. The third hit may use a stronger pose, impact flash, and heavier verified sound while remaining a light-combo finisher. Misses use a distinct cool-colored whiff indicator at the contact instant and no dummy flash, health movement, or counter increase.

The HUD remains sparse: dummy health and numeric value at the top center, accepted-hit count directly below, a short contextual Hit/Miss/Recovery message near the reticle area, and controls near the lower corners. Touch Attack is large enough for a thumb and positioned away from Reset; Reset requires a deliberate tap and has a clear label. Desktop displays compact binding hints without duplicating oversized touch controls. UI transitions should be quick and readable, with health tweening only after accepted server damage and no speculative client-side count changes.
